title: squish: choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the folded road map. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Folded Road Map
options.lineage: pocket road maps and city plans that fold a huge sheet into a palm-sized panel
options.thesis: Compression is folding: a big image folds down to pocket size, and the saving reads as a map scale.
options.viewport: Cobalt map-cover header with squish and EN/HR switch; left panel drop zone plus format, quality and size controls; right a file table where every row carries a scale bar reading like 1 : 4.2.
options.risk: Fold creases as decoration turn costume if they stop marking real layout panels.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale contrast: the total saving is the one huge figure, every label stays small.
Every file state is a physical fold state: flat (queued), folding (working), folded (done), torn corner (error).
Fold creases are the layout grid; the page reflows by whole panels.
File size sits on one fixed visual ramp everywhere it appears.

options.label: Vacuum Storage Bag
options.lineage: vacuum-seal storage bags printed with before/after volume
options.thesis: Your images go in the bag, the air comes out, the bag prints how much smaller it got.
options.viewport: White ground, orange zip-seal strip as the top bar; a large bag-shaped drop zone that tightens around the thumbnails; a printed packaging panel lists before/after per file.
options.risk: Closest to familiar product-tool looks; the bag outline must earn its keep or it reads as a generic rounded drop zone.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.lineage: streaming catalog rows of poster tiles
options.thesis: Your batch as a wall of tiles; the focused image grows and shows its new size while the rest dims.
options.viewport: Dark ground, settings bar on top, batch as a tile row; focused tile expanded with format chip and before/after size.
options.case: Everyone knows this wall, so audience identification beats the map; product clarity is weaker because settings sit outside the tiles.
options.risk: Dark, image-led tool looks like many media apps; settings can get lost behind the tiles.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.thesis: One slider morphs the whole page live.
options.case: General users do not identify with type specimens; clarity ties at best.
options.risk: Reads as a type tool, not an image tool.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Settings as acetate leaves over coloured divider boards.
options.case: Loses on both axes: unfamiliar object, heavier navigation than a one-page tool needs.
options.kept: A physical vocabulary for every state.
options.risk: Navigation overhead for a single-task page.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The grid itself is the visible armature.
options.viewport: Grid-built display letters over small grotesk.
options.case: Loses both axes: designer reference, adds no meaning to compression.
options.kept: Visible grid as structure, not ornament.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.thesis: Images as registered plates on near-white stock.
options.case: Loses both axes: elegant, but a general user sees a gallery, not a converter.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Files as stars, size as magnitude.
options.viewport: Batch plotted as dots that shrink after compression.
options.case: Loses both axes: poetic, but a dot field reads slower than a file list.
options.kept: A fixed ramp that encodes size.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean converter page like Squoosh or TinyPNG, executed with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Centered dashed drop zone, settings row below, result list with sizes.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other converter by design.
